stories.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, a company that makes AI tools, promised to give 5% of its shares to a fund that supports public good projects. Think of it like a business owner setting aside part of their profits for charity.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people focused on AI ethics. If you use Anthropic's AI tools, this doesn't change how they work or cost.

stories.title: The AI industry’s gigantic debts are making investors nervous
stories.simple_summary: AI companies have borrowed a lot of money and spent huge amounts of cash to build their technology. Now investors are worried these companies might not make enough money to pay back what they owe.
stories.why_it_matters: This could affect AI tool prices or availability if companies run into trouble, but that's not happening yet.

stories.title: A woman was arrested in Philly for blocking a delivery robot
stories.simple_summary: A woman in Philadelphia was arrested after she blocked a small robot that delivers food orders, because she was worried the robot was taking jobs away from human delivery workers.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a real concern people have about robots replacing workers, though it's still rare for this to lead to arrests.

stories.title: Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character.AI’s workforce
stories.simple_summary: Disney is hiring most of the workers from a company called Character.AI. However, another company could still make a higher offer to hire them instead.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to people in the tech industry. It shows Disney is investing in AI, but it doesn't change anything for ordinary people.

stories.title: Elder Gong Calls for Moral Compass in Age of AI at G20 Interfaith Forum
stories.simple_summary: A religious leader spoke at a world forum about the need for values and ethics when developing AI technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a general statement about AI and values. It doesn't affect your day-to-day life or business.

stories.title: Man’s Meta Muse Agent Sends Him Message So Bizarre That He Permanently Quits
stories.simple_summary: A man stopped using a Meta AI assistant after it sent him a strange message that upset him.
stories.why_it_matters: AI tools sometimes make odd mistakes, and this shows one example of that happening.

stories.title: Anthropic’s proposed AI safety bill only kicks in if 50 deaths or $1 billion in damages are on the line — proposal would effectively make the Commerce Department the only agency capable of stopping an AI model
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic suggested a new rule where AI systems would only face government action if they caused at least 50 deaths or $1 billion in damage. This would give the Commerce Department power to act.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a proposal about how AI should be regulated. It mostly matters to tech companies and policymakers, not to everyday people yet.

stories.title: World Bank says ‘small AI’ could transform developing countries
stories.simple_summary: The World Bank says smaller, simpler AI tools could help developing countries solve problems in farming, health, and education more cheaply than expensive AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI doesn't always need to be complicated and expensive. It could help more people around the world.

stories.title: Epstein gave $100K to UNM for artificial intelligence research in 2001
stories.simple_summary: A university received $100,000 from a donor in 2001 to research artificial intelligence. The donor had a troubled past.
stories.why_it_matters: This is historical news about where research money came from. It doesn't affect you now.

stories.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
stories.simple_summary: Meta (the company behind Facebook) changed the words in its terms of service that people worried might let them take content from websites to train their AI. Meta says this didn't change what they actually do.
stories.why_it_matters: If you share things online, Meta may still use them to train AI, but they're not changing their actual practices.

stories.title: Bricklayer, 49, travels 1,200 miles for dream girl — only to discover she’s AI-generated
stories.simple_summary: A man traveled across the country hoping to meet someone he liked online, but discovered that the person was not real. An AI had created fake pictures instead.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a reminder to be careful about who you meet online. AI can now create fake photos and videos, so verify people are real before trusting them.

stories.title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, an AI company, now has more experienced workers and spends more time in meetings than it did before.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors following the company. It doesn't change their products.
